short: Catherine of Aragon was the first wife of Henry VIII, whose refusal to accept an annulment triggered the English Reformation.
full:
The daughter of Isabella and Ferdinand of Spain, Catherine of Aragon first came to England to marry Arthur, Prince of Wales. After Arthur's sudden death, she married his younger brother, Henry VIII, serving as a popular queen and even acting as regent during his military campaigns in France. Despite multiple pregnancies, she produced only one surviving child, the future Mary I, leading Henry to seek an annulment in order to secure a male heir.

Catherine mounted a fierce legal and moral defence, refusing to quietly retire to a nunnery and insisting she was Henry's only lawful wife. With the Pope unwilling to grant the annulment, Henry broke with Rome, declaring the marriage invalid in 1533. Banished from court and separated from her daughter, Catherine lived her final years in isolated, dignified defiance, considering herself the rightful queen until her death in 1536.
